Nancy J. Lyford Adams
BERLIN — Nancy J. Lyford Adams, 64, passed away on December 29, 2025 at the McClure Miller Respite House in Colchester, Vermont.
Nancy was born July 30,1961 to Ann French Lyford and Mage A. Lyford in Lebanon New Hampshire.
She graduated Woodstock Union High School in 1979, then attended Champlain and Trinity colleges. Nancy worked as a human resource Manager her entire career, retiring from Cabot Creamery.
Nancy enjoyed gardening, trips to Maine, country drives, watching NASCAR and the New England Patriots. She was a member of Enough Ministries.
Nancy was predeceased by her mother, father and sister Carol L Rogenski. She is survived by her brothers Brian M. Lyford and Steven E. Lyford, sister Laura L. Black and many nieces, nephews and cousins.
There will be no calling hours. In the spring there will be a celebration of Nancy’s life.
Donations may be sent to the McClure Miller Respite House in Colchester, Vermont in Nancy’s name. Please visit www.awrfh.com to share your memories and condolences.

Marcia Anne Andres
MIDDLESEX — Marcia Anne Andres passed away peacefully on January 5th, 2026, in the comfort of the home she shared with her beloved children and grandchildren. Marcie was born on May 23, 1946, in Saint Paul, Minnesota, the daughter of Sibel (Penny) and Robert Andres. She grew up in Walla Walla, Washington, and spent her childhood downhill skiing and dancing ballet.
Throughout high school, she ran her own ballet school and worked as a manager and short-order cook at a drive-in. Somehow she also found time to study, continue her own dance practice, captain the cheerleading squad, and be elected homecoming queen.
Marcie attended the University of Montana and graduated in 1968. After college, Marcie hitchhiked around Europe, lugging her ski boots on her back before landing a job as a chambermaid at a ski chalet in the Swiss Alps for the winter.
When she came back to the US she joined the teacher corps, serving in Seattle, Washington, where she taught eighth grade while earning two master's degrees in education. In 1970, she met an East Coast transplant named Larry Mandell. They moved back east so that Larry could attend law school in Boston. Marcie got a job teaching reading at ABCD in South Boston.
Marcie and Larry moved to Vermont in 1974 and got married at the Greenhurst Inn in Bethel, Vermont.
Marcie taught sixth grade at Williamstown Elementary School before becoming a beloved teacher at Rumney Elementary School in Middlesex for twenty-five years.
She was a curious, creative, and student-centered educator, always seeking out new ways to engage her “kids” and make learning accessible and relevant to them. She particularly loved -- and excelled at -- figuring out ways to reach students who felt that school “was not for them.” She helped create the garden program at Rumney and later built a hydroponic living machine in her sixth-grade classroom.
After retiring from Rumney, Marcie became co-director of Central Vermont Adult Education, where she tutored English language learners and developed personalized strategies to help adults learn to read even after decades of frustration. As she had with generations of Rumney students, Marcie gave her students her all, dedicating hours to finding them housing and other supports.
In 1976, Marcie and Larry bought an old farmhouse in Middlesex. In 2016, tired of shoveling and mowing the lawn, Marcie and Larry sold the house to Bekah and her family and moved into Montpelier, where Marcie, a voracious reader, enjoyed walking to the library to check out armloads of books.
Marcie loved being a “Bubbie” to her grandchildren, Loren and Calla. During the pandemic, Marcie was a lifeline for Bekah and her family. With daycares closed, she enrolled Loren and Calla in “Bubbie School.” Every day brought a new lesson plan tied to a letter of the alphabet with lots of messy hands-on fun.
Marcie continued to be an important part of Loren and Calla’s lives, picking them up from school, chauffeuring them to their afterschool activities, and playing hours of games with them.
Marcie is survived by her two children Bekah and Jeff, Bekah’s two children, Loren and Calla, her sister Cathy and her husband Jim, her brothers- and sisters-in-law Richard and Marilyn Mandell, and Seth and Sherri Mandell as well as her beloved nieces and nephews and their kids.
Marcie will be missed by her beloved family as well as wonderful lifelong friends and generations of Vermont kids who, through her creativity, discovered that they too loved -- and deserved to love -- learning.
A funeral service will be held on Friday, January 9th at 1:30 pm at Guare & Sons in Montpelier. In lieu of flowers, people who love and appreciate Marcie can make contributions to Central Vermont Adult Education, the Rumney PTNO, Central Vermont Home Health and Hospice, Public Assets Institute, or Circus Smirkus.

Agnes L. Aubertin
BERLIN — Agnes L. (Corbett) Aubertin passed away at Woodridge Nursing Home, Berlin, VT, on January 3, 2026, at the age of 95, meeting her goal of living to the same age of her mom's passing. She previously resided for over seven years at Heaton Woods, Montpelier, VT.
Born in Barre City on December 30, 1930, she was the daughter of the late James J. Corbett and Helen Zoe (Frechette) Corbett.
Agnes was a graduate of Spaulding High School Class of 1949. She worked at Sprague Electric and later as a bookkeeper for many area businesses, and had volunteered for 22 years at CVMC gift shop.
On December 30, 1955, she married Edward D. Aubertin at the Universalist Church in Barre. They lived in Barre, Middlesex, and East Montpelier, and in 1968 purchased a home on Third Street in Barre. Ed passed away on August 1, 1994.
Survivors include her daughter, Judith M. (Aubertin) Dibbell and husband Richard of Lake Wales, Florida; granddaughter Jody (MacDonald) Marshall and husband Eric of Manchester, TN, as well as many nieces and nephews.
Besides her parents, husband, and five siblings, she was predeceased by her son, James D. Aubertin on August 24, 2016.
To honor her wishes, there will be no calling hours or funeral service. Memorial contributions in her memory can be made to the Aldrich Library, 6 Washington Street, Barre, VT 05641.
Arrangements are in the care of Pruneau-Polli Funeral Home, 58 Summer Street in Barre.
Those wishing to express online condolences may do so at www.pruneaupollifuneralhome.com.

David M. Bolda
SCARBOROUGH, ME — David Michael Bolda died at home in Scarborough, Maine, on December 13, 2025, due to congestive heart failure. He was born on November 12, 1951, in Alexandria, VA, the son of Frank J. Bolda and Catherine E. Hynes Bolda. The family moved north when David was 5, and he attended grade school in Poughkeepsie, NY, before moving to Raleigh, NC, in 1966.
David was appointed to the US Naval Academy in 1969 and transferred to NC State University as a Thomas J Watson Scholar, graduating in 1973. After extended travel in Europe, he returned to NC and worked in the Research Triangle area before entering the University of North Carolina-Chapel Hill, School of Public Health. He completed his Master of Science in Public Health in 1978 and began his career as an industrial hygienist with the Vermont Department of Health, VOSHA program. In Vermont, he met and later married (1987) Elise L. Johnston (Lisa) in Montpelier.
In 1984, David and Lisa moved to Hillsborough/Durham, NC, where David passed his CIH exam and worked with three consulting groups, PES, ELB, and EI. David continued his pastimes of racquet sports, golfing, and windsurfing. He only had to be rescued by the Coast Guard once.
In 1995, they moved to Maine, and David continued to work with EI before taking a job with SafetyWorks at the Maine Department of Labor in 1999. After his retirement in 2011, David volunteered and participated as a learner with the Goodwill LifeWorks Program for several years.
As friends from David's UNC lads group say, Dave led a complicated life. He lived with bipolar disorder that he managed with medication and a few inpatient stays; Parkinson’s, which took a toll on many of his functions yet spared his good humor and capabilities in many other ways; and scoliosis, which caused episodic and sometimes severe back pain. David was ever grateful for his team of caring clinicians (Karen Dmytrasz /Stacey Farrington, Emily Erickson, Bernard Gordon, Aline Iskandar/Leana Thomas, William Jeanblanc/Heather Emerson, and the amazing Oliver Phillips) and his therapists (the magical Bill Anderson and Tess Boyle, Emma Holder, Bonnie Topham, Amy and Cody). David greatly appreciated the strong arms and caring hearts of JP Phaneuf, man of many talents, the stellar women who provided care 24/7 (Amie, Becky, Bella, Gabrielle, Jewel, Krista, Lauren and Ribka), the wonderful nurses and shower aces from Northern Lights Home Health and Hospice, and Chef Zoe.
David was locally known as the Millipede Whisperer, due to his hours and skill at this video game. He first played it in the ‘80s at a Durham arcade. His family bought him the machine for his 40th birthday. He set this year’s best score--over 49,000--on his birthday.
David is survived by his wife Lisa and their cat Bert, younger sister Suzanne Neal (Tom) of Appleton, WI, and their family: in Minneapolis, son Tom Neal (Megan Powell), granddaughter Margot, and daughter Michelle Naylor (William) and grandchildren Hakon and Signe; and in Milwaukee, daughter Mary Turek and grandson Wesley. He is also survived by his youngest sister, Cheryl Toole (Bob), and son Shane Toole of Raleigh. Other survivors are his
sister-in-law Anna Johnston in NC, nephew Christopher Monte, who lived with David & Lisa in NC, and Peter Monte (the nephew he most enjoyed trouncing at racquetball) and their families in NC and TX; sister-in-law Francine Johnston in MA, and nephews Demian and Morgan Johnston and their families in CT.
David is predeceased by his brother Donald F. Bolda, his mother, Catherine, and father, Frank, his Johnston in-laws, Morna, Herbie, and Gregory, and his canine companions Jeeves, Nigel, Riley, Rex, and Earnest Tucker Bolda.
He will be remembered as a witty, kind, and gentle man.
David’s cremains will be interred at the Middlesex Center Cemetery in Vermont.
He would want you to save your money, but if you are so inclined, memorial contributions can be sent to: Parkinson’s Voice Project https://parkinsonvoiceproject.org/donate/ in honor of his steadfast Speech Pathologist, Tess Boyle SLP.

Stephanette Boudreault
BARRE — Stephanette Boudreault, 90, of Barre, Vermont, passed away peacefully on December 29, 2025, at The Lincoln House with family by her side. Born October 6, 1935, in Lac St. Jean, Quebec, Canada, Stephanette was the daughter of Louis-Joseph and Marie-Louise Boily. She was one of nine siblings. Before meeting the love of her life, Jacques, Stephanette worked as a seamstress. They were married in Coaticook, Quebec and then moved to Central Vermont in 1965 with their three children.
Stephanette’s gift was to take care of others which enabled her to build a successful career as a home health aide for over 40 years. She was known for creating beautiful holiday decorations, many of which still hang in St. Monica’s Church where she was a devout member. From decorating Christmas wreaths to painting ceramics, she was a talented crafter. Mimi was a devoted mother, grandmother and great-grandmother, who loved and cherished spending time with family above all else. She was known for filling the halls with her laughter and singing.
Her great-grandchildren noted that she will be most remembered for her humor, fiery spirit, stubbornness, kindness, caring nature, affection, love, and creativity. Stephanette, along with her husband Jacques, was dedicated to supporting and caring for family and friends, they were known for their selflessness and generosity. She enjoyed spending time outdoors, especially at the family camp in Norton, Vermont, and going for car rides with Jacques; she enjoyed having breakfast with friends at Soups and Greens or Wayside, or with her family at Café Central in Coaticook, Québec; attending her children, grandchildren and great grandchildren’s events, including military, school and sports; visiting her family in Canada; crafting, baking, and shopping.
Stephanette touched countless lives and has left a huge void in many people’s hearts. Although the family has lost their matriarch, her legacy will remain in their hearts forever as she watches over them from heaven.
Stephanette is survived by her three children, Mario (Rhonda Richards), Gilles (Victoria Canas) and Sylvie (Fred Blanchard); grandchildren, Christopher Bylow (Sara Calcagni), Jennifer (Colt Knipp), Katie Bylow (Travis Welch), Fae Boudreault, Alexis Blanchard and Isabella Boudreault; her great-grandchildren, Kaylee and Taylor Welch, Jacob and Lauren Bylow, and Amelia and Violet Knipp. Also survived by her sister Jacqueline (Jean-Pierre Laliberte); and sisters-in-law Rachel Quintal, Marthe Tremblay, Jeannine (Lionel Richard), Claudette Beaudin, Denise Boily, and Angele Boily.
Stephanette is reunited with her husband of 60 years, Jacques Boudreault and her parents, Louis-Joseph and Marie-Louise Boily; her sisters, Hermance Boily (Roger Dufault), Pauline Boily (first husband Andre Fortin, second husband Germain Martel) and infant sister Andree; her brothers, Jules Boily, Gerard Boily, Edgar Boily (Liliane), Yvon Boily (Bernadette), Yvan Boily; brothers-in-law, Marcel Boudreault (Camille), Aurelien “Raymond” Boudreault, Edward Quintal, Camille Boudreault (Madeleine), and Richard Tremblay.
A Mass of Christian burial will be celebrated at St. Monica’s Church in Barre at a later date, followed by a graveside memorial to be determined. Arrangements are in the care of the
Pruneau-Polli Funeral Home, 58 Summer St., Barre Vermont. Those wishing to send online condolences may do so at: www.pruneaupollifuneralhome.com.

Theodore J. Cochran
PLAINFIELD — Theodore James Cochran, “Tad”, 64, a longtime resident of Walker Lane, passed away on Friday, December 19, 2025, at the Brigham and Women’s Hospital in Boston.
Born on January 29, 1961, in Lakehurst, New Jersey, he was the son of Kenneth and Janice (McCarthy) Cochran. He attended elementary school in Orange and graduated from Spaulding High school in 1980.
Following his schooling, Tad went to work for Kinfolk Memorials, where he worked as a master stone cutter for 42 years before retiring in 2024. He also ran Big ‘C’ Sugaring with his father and sons for 23 years.
Throughout his life, Tad had many hobbies and interests. Those included hunting, especially going on trips to Ohio with his son Elliott and friends, helping to process deer and wild game for himself and friends, playing cards, spending new years eve at the Bibeau’s, attending feeds at the Tucker’s hunting camp, going on fishing charters on Lake Champlain and just being outdoors enjoying the “Nature of his Mountain”.
Survivors include his sons Sean Cochran and Elliott Cochran and his wife, Lauren; his mother Janice Cochran; his grandchildren Aislinn, Declan and Elijah Cochran; his siblings Kenneth Cochran, Jr., Karen Heinlein and Sari Calevro. He also leaves life partner Nola Howder and her daughter Skylar as well as numerous nieces and nephews.
He was predeceased by his father Kenneth Cochran, Sr.
A graveside service to honor and celebrate Tad’s life will be held on Sunday, May 17, 2026, in the Wilson Cemetery in Barre Town. There are no calling hours.
Arrangements are by Hooker Whitcomb Funeral Home, 7 Academy Street, Barre. For a memorial guestbook, please visit www.hookerwhitcomb.com.

Marjorie Couillard
WEBSTERVILLE — Marjorie Couillard, 94, passed away on Saturday, December 27, 2025, at Barre Gardens Nursing and Rehabilitation Center.
Born on January 25, 1931, in Barre Town, she was the daughter of Charles and Ethel (Fuller) Payne. At the age of three, Marjorie’s family moved to Washington where she grew up.
She attended Washington Elementary School, Barre Town Elementary School, Spaulding High School and graduated from Williamstown High School.
On November 6, 1954, she married Willard Couillard in the St. Sylvester Catholic Church in Websterville. Following their marriage, they first lived in Barre, before moving to Graniteville and eventually settling in Websterville.
While living in Washington, Marjorie attended the Washington Baptist Church and was a youth group member and sang in the choir. She was also a member of the Barre Baptist Church and a long-time member of the Graniteville Presbyterian Church including serving on the board of trustees. Lastly, she attended the Websterville Baptist Church. Marjorie was involved in the PTA and girl scouts while her children were young.
She worked for the former Montgomery Wards retiring after 20 years of service.
In her spare time, she enjoyed her family, church, reading, walking around the neighborhood, cross-country skiing, traveling, and camping. She especially enjoyed summer vacations on Higgins Beach in Maine.
Survivors include her three children Charmane McKenzie (Steve), Chuck Couillard (Rhonda), and Dan Couillard (Sandy), and her grandchildren Tara Partlow (Josh), Ryan McKenzie (Amy Morse), Racheal Hill (Jason), and Matt Couillard (Jasmin) as well as six great grandchildren.
In addition to her parents, she was predeceased by her husband Willard Couillard, her grandson Daniel W. Couillard, her sisters Lida Mugford (Wayne) and Mae Braman (Howard), and her brother Vern Payne and her special uncle Homer Fuller.
The service to honor and celebrate her life will be held on Saturday, January 24, 2026, at 11:00 a.m. in the Websterville Baptist Church, 143 Church Hill Road, Websterville. There are no calling hours.
Marjorie’s family would like to give a special thank you to the Barre Gardens for their compassion and exceptional care.
In lieu of flowers memorial contributions may be made to the Vermont Foodbank, 33 Parker Road, Barre, VT 05641.
Arrangements are by Hooker Whitcomb Funeral Home, 7 Academy Street, Barre. For a memorial guestbook, please visit www.hookerwhitcomb.com.

William Gilwee
BARRE — William Gilwee, 86, a longtime resident of Ledge Drive, passed away peacefully on Tuesday, January 6, 2026, at the Central Vermont Medical Center in Berlin.
A Mass of Christian Burial to honor William’s life will be held on Wednesday, January 21, 2026, at 11:00 a.m. in St. Monica Catholic Church on Summer Street in Barre. Burial will take place at a time to be announced in the spring.
A complete obituary will be published in a future edition of the Times Argus.
Arrangements are in the care of Hooker Whitcomb Funeral Home.

Joyce E. Hastings
BARRE — Joyce E. Hastings, 82, of Barre, VT, passed away Friday, January 2, 2026, at CVMC in Berlin surrounded by her family. Born September 4, 1943, in Barre to George and Pauline (Edson) Willette. She attended Marion High School. On May 23, 1964 she married Clark Hastings Jr. They made their home in Barre.
Joyce was employed at Sprague Electric, Rainforest Crunch, VT Butter & Cheese, and S.B. Electronics.
Joyce’s life was her family. She was a devoted mother, grandmother and great grandmother. She spent her days going on adventures with her children, dancing to country music, playing with all her grandbabies and making soup every Sunday for family brunch.
She is survived by her children, Clark Hastings III and his partner Johanne, Tammy Maurice and her husband Marc, Corrina Garbacik and her husband Joel, Tina Priddy and her partner Alexis, Sue Priddy and her husband Wayne, and Dawn Sayers, 15 grandchildren, 17 greatgrandchildren, sisters Shirley Schlossin and her partner Carl, Norma Lalime, brother Donald Tofani and his wife Dee, and many nieces and nephews.
She is predeceased by her parents George and Pauline, her husband Clark, her siblings Larry Edson, Winfred Willette, Charles Willette, Richard Willette, William Willette, Anna Dukette, Janice Stephenson and her grandson Jayvin Maurice.
A Mass of Christian Burial to celebrate Joyces life will be held on Thursday January 8, 2026 at 11:00 AM at St. Monica Church In Barre. A private burial will follow in the spring at Fairview Cemetery in Hardwick Vt.
In lieu of flowers, donations can be made in her honor to the Leukemia Research Foundation, 191 Waukegan Road, Suite 105 Northfield, Illinois 60093.
Arrangements are in the care of Pruneau-Polli Funeral Home in Barre.
Those wishing to express online condolences may do so at: www.pruneaupollifuneralhome.com.

Edward C. Hutchins
WEBSTERVILLE — Edward Conrad Hutchins, 90, of Church Hill Road, passed away on Tuesday, December 9, 2025, at home peacefully.
Born on May 3, 1935, in East Barre, he was the son of Leon L. and Hattie (Moore) Hutchins. Eddie attended elementary school in East Barre and Spaulding High School.
On January 21, 1956, he married Janet Lawson in Graniteville. Following their marriage, they made their home in Websterville.
Eddie worked in the granite industry for 50 years. He enjoyed hunting, fishing, horseshoes, and playing cards.
Survivors include his sons Mark Hutchins and his wife, Suzanne of Barre, VT; Michael Hutchins of Burlington, VT; and Peter Hutchins and his wife, Pam of South Carolina; his grandchildren Jowana and her husband, Drew; Jeff and his wife, Natalie; Chad and his wife, Caitlin; Jason, and Kurt, his great-grandchildren Cole, Jackson, Hannah, Laine, Henry, and Ira; and his sister-in-law Beverly Lawson and his brother-in-law Richard LaCross as well as many nieces and nephews. Also, special friends Ike Chase, and Ricky, and Patty Hutchins.
In addition to his parents, he was predeceased by his wife Janet, and his grandson, Eric.
A graveside service to honor and celebrate his life will be held at the convenience of his family in Wilson Cemetery in Lower Websterville. There are no calling hours.
Arrangements are by Hooker Whitcomb Funeral Home, 7 Academy Street, Barre. For a memorial guestbook, please visit www.hookerwhitcomb.com.

Jeannine M. LaCroix
BARRE — Jeannine Maurice LaCroix passed away peacefully December 25, 2025. She was born April 4, 1931, at home at the family farm in Hardwick, VT. She was the daughter of Raoul and Delia Maurice and was the third of six children. Her parents moved to Barre when she was three. She was educated at St. Monica’s School and graduated from Spaulding High School in 1949. She was a devoted wife to her beloved husband, Raymond for 63 years and mother to their seven children, grandmother to 22 grandchildren and great grandmother to 17 great grand children. Jeannine loved to cook traditional French meals for her family and friends, always making visitors to their home feel very welcome. She was an impeccable housekeeper with a gift for growing flowers and vegetables. Their door was always open to their friends and family to come in and share a meal or just for a visit. Jeannine was a member of St. Monica Church, Ladies of the Knights of Columbus, Catholic Daughters of the Americas (serving as Regent, 1983-1985), Dame de St. Anne, Montpelier Senior Center, and Barre Senior Center. She enjoyed rug hooking, crochet, knitting, making Pierce cutout lamp shades, sewing, canning, camping , cross country skiing, snowshoeing, hiking, dancing, making puzzles, playing cards, Mahjongg and reading. Her travels included Europe, Alaska, Hawaii, the Caribbean, Canada and the United States.
Jeannine was predeceased by her parents and two brothers (Fernand and Leo Maurice) and her husband, Raymond LaCroix. She is survived by her seven children Leo LaCroix of Woodstock, VT, Luke and his wife Jo Ann LaCroix of Williston, VT, Lise and her husband Roland Pitts of Lakewood, CO, Maurice and his wife Cyndie LaCroix of Ballston, NY, Louis and his wife Tracy LaCroix of Matthews, NC, Marielle and her husband Gary Fitch of Roswell, GA and Michelle and her husband Michael Matteis of East Burke, VT and her 22 grandchildren Erin and Alex Lahammer, Nate and Tick LaCroix, Ian and Mary LaCroix, Keith and Rae-Ann LaCroix, Melissa and Mike Barron, Christina LaCroix, Ben and Crystal Pitts, Jessica Pitts, Emily and Todd Ipsen, Sarah Pitts, Ryan and Robin LaCroix, Kyle and Annie LaCroix, Haylee LaCroix, Kelsy LaCroix, Taylor LaCroix and wife Elyse, Cameron LaCroix, Avery LaCroix, Ashleigh Fitch, Andrew Fitch, Audrey Fitch, Olivia Matteis, and Nicholas Matteis and 17 great grandchildren.
Jeannine always had a positive attitude in everything she did. Her recent activities include attending St. Monica’s Church, saying the rosary, functions at the Barre Senior Center(meals, cards, games, Book Club, and trips including a cruise to Bermuda with her daughter Lise), playing piano, gardening, canning, entertaining, playing cards with family and friends, exercising at Barre Rehab Center, walking her dog Libby and enjoying sitting out by the fire pit reading the paper or on the phone with one of her kids. She also enjoyed special vacations and reunions in Canada, Vermont, North Carolina, Georgia, Colorado and Maine with her family.
Since 2021, she has resided in Woodstock, GA (where her daughter Marielle lives) she loved her time with Holbrook community and participating in all the activities while always making others around her smile.
Her life mattered and her love does not end, it will carry on through generations of all who knew her.
A celebration of life will be at a later date.

June A. (Lloyd) Manning
MONTPELIER — June Alma (Lloyd) Manning, 75, a longtime resident of Montpelier Vermont, passed away after a brief illness on Christmas Eve at Mission Care of Bennington.
June was born on May 27th, 1950 in Magog Quebec to Victor and Therese (Metivier) Lloyd, one of three daughters. Born into a farming family, she often spoke fondly about growing up on the farm, caring for the cows and riding horses.
June attended schools in East Calais and Montpelier. She married her first husband, Kenneth Mills in 1969 and they had three children together. During these years they lived in Troy VT, South Dakota, New Mexico and Texas.
In 1977 June returned home to Vermont with her children and began her lifelong employment with the State of Vermont retiring in 2005. She was most proud of her position as administrative assistant for the Vermont State Police.
In 1984 June married the love of her life Neil Manning. They enjoyed several happy years together fishing, playing horseshoes and watching baseball (NY Yankees for her/Boston Red Sox for Neil) until his passing.
June had several hobbies through the years. In early years she took flying lessons and successfully executed her first solo flight. In later years she taught herself to play guitar and cross-stitching, creating many beautiful works of art for family, friends and co-workers.
June was known for her helping way, always paying attention and identifying a need that a neighbor or friend might have and giving what she could to help. Whether it be a versa cart for shopping, a vacuum, healing lotions or food. She just wanted to make things better for others if she could.
June is survived by her son Victor Mills of Sutherline, OR, daughter Victoria Jewett of East Barre, VT, granddaughters Shelby Jewett of Dover, NH and Aliyah Jewett of East Barre, VT, sister Margaret Bowen of East Calais, VT, twin sister Judy Taplin of Montpelier, VT, as well as three nieces. She was predeceased by her parents, infant daughter Margaret Ann Mills in 1978 and her husband Neil Manning in 2013.
A graveside service will be held in the spring at the Pine Grove Cemetery in Newport VT. In lieu of flowers contributions can be made to Veteran’s Place in Northfield, VT.

Doris J. Martin
THE VILLAGES, FL — Doris J. “Jean” Martin, 77, passed away on December 4, 2025, in The Villages, Florida. Born on November 15, 1948, in Barre, Vermont, Jean lived a life marked by dedication to her profession and a deep interest in family heritage.
A graduate of Spaulding High School’s Class of 1966, Jean went on to earn her degree from Champlain College in Burlington in 1968. She began her career with a CPA firm in Burlington and went on to hold positions at Better Home Construction in Barre, Goddard College, the Duxbury school district in Vermont, and NCS in Houston, Texas.
In 1986, Jean returned to Vermont and continued her accounting work with the Agency of Transportation for the State of Vermont until her retirement in 2013. Her strong work ethic and commitment to excellence were evident throughout her career.
Jean was the devoted wife of the late Edward L. Martin and the cherished mother of Edward R. Martin and his wife Brandie Russell-Martin; Jeremy A. Martin and his wife Casey Martin; and Lori A. Martin. She was a proud grandmother to Britny Chamberlin, Kylee Pierce, Nathaniel Pierce, Taylor Haggett, Kyle Martin, Bailee Martin, Shawn Martin, Broc Haggett, Jason Martin, and D’aja Martin.
She is also remembered by her siblings: William T. Philip; Debra J. Marvin and husband Dwight; Charles E. Philip and wife Liz; James F. Philip and wife Julie Philip; as well as numerous cousins, nieces, nephews, and great-grandchildren.
Jean was predeceased by her husband Edward L. Martin; her parents William T. Philip and Ella M. Philip; and her sister Donna J. Baker.
Jean had a passion for genealogy and took great care in preserving family history. She also enjoyed following NASCAR and had a lifelong love of horses.
May her memory bring comfort to all who were touched by her life.
A memorial service will be held at the Wesley United Methodist Church in Waterbury, Vermont, on Saturday, January 10, 2026, starting at 11 am. After the service, light refreshments will be provided downstairs in the church.
Burial in final resting place will be held in the spring in Plainmont Cemetery in East Montpelier, Vermont.
Perkins-Parker Funeral Home in Waterbury is overseeing arrangements.

Edward L. Martin
LEESBURG, FL — Edward Leslie “Ed” Martin, 75, passed away on November 24, 2025, in Leesburg, Florida. Born on August 21, 1950, in Barre, Vermont, Ed lived a life marked by dedication to family, hard work, and unwavering generosity.
A proud graduate of Spaulding High School’s Class of 1969 in Barre, Ed went on to attend St. Johnsbury Trade School in St. Johnsbury, Vermont, graduating in 1970. Shortly after completing his education, he served with honor in the Vermont National Guard until his discharge in 1973.
Ed began his professional journey working at the Windsor prison in Windsor, Vermont. He later transitioned into construction and concrete work before moving to Texas, where he was employed by Quality Cabinets in both Houston and Dallas. In 1986, he returned to his beloved Vermont and joined Ben & Jerry’s. He concluded his career at the Vermont State Hospital, retiring in 2013 after years of dedicated service.
Throughout his life, Ed was known for putting others before himself. His selflessness was especially evident in the care he provided for his wife, Doris J. Martin—always prioritizing her well-being above his own. His love for his children and grandchildren was boundless and deeply felt by all who knew him.
Ed is survived by his devoted wife, Doris; their three children: Edward R. Martin and his wife, Brandie Russell-Martin; Jeremy A. Martin and his wife, Casey Martin; and Lori A. Martin. He also leaves behind his brother George S. Martin and wife Joyce Martin; sister Connie Murray and cherished grandchildren: Britny Chamberlin, Kylee Pierce, Nathaniel Pierce, Taylor Haggett, Kyle Martin, Bailee Martin, Shawn Martin, Broc Haggett, Jason Martin, and D’aja Martin; as well as numerous cousins, nieces, nephews, and great-grandchildren who will carry forward his memory.
He was predeceased by his parents, Leslie W. Martin and Elva M. Martin.
Outside of work and family life, Ed found joy in fishing and watching NASCAR races. He especially treasured time spent visiting with family—a priority that remained central throughout his life. A man of deep commitment to community and fellowship, Ed was a proud member of the Masons at Winooski Lodge #49 in Waterbury and a member of the Mount Sinai Shriners.
Ed’s legacy is one of quiet strength and enduring love—a man who gave freely of himself so that others might thrive.

MONTPELIER — Barry E. McPhee, 62, of Montpelier, Vermont, passed away on December 15, 2025, at the McClure Miller Respite House in Colchester, Vermont, following a short battle with cancer. He left us peacefully, surrounded by loved ones.
He was a 1981 graduate of Roxbury Latin High School in Boston, and went on to receive a B.S. from Boston University, and an M.S. from the University of Vermont. Barry was a passionate advocate for the environment and engaged in multiple volunteer and leadership positions over the years. He was always up for outdoor activities, such as body surfing at Hampton Beach, hiking the Green Mountains, biking solo or with friends, canoeing, walking his dog while working out in Montpelier’s Hubbard Park, or throwing a frisbee with friends.
He will be remembered for his humor, his appreciation of music and literature, and his deep love for his family and friends. Barry’s idea of a perfect day was taking a long bike ride on a crisp autumn day, followed by a simple meal that absolutely did not include any tomatoes or asparagus, and finally winding down with a beer on his back deck with loved ones.
He is survived by his wife Sarah McGinnis, daughter Susannah McPhee, grandson Cameron Johnson, his mother Carole Cody, brother Christopher McPhee, sister Maryellen Frawley, and a large and loving group of extended family and friends.

Christopher J. Sanden
NORTHFIELD — Christopher Joel Sanden, 65, passed away September 2025 and was found looking peaceful at his home in Northfield, VT. Chris was born March 23, 1960 in Washington DC, the son of Lewis & Jean Sanden.
After graduating from Annandale High School, Chris received several certifications specializing in various areas such as Advanced Steam Engineering, Commercial Burner and Controls, and countless others. Over the span of his 41-year career his talents and service were recognized and well respected. Beginning his career as a Journeyman & service technician, over the years he rose to Supervisor positions that created a difference at Susquehanna University and ultimately Norwich University in Northfield, VT. Chris thrived on teaching and sharing his knowledge. He loved taking the time to give tours to interested individuals and groups and had kept several thank you notes as mementos. Chris’ expertise of boiler systems and his passion for not only his trade but for those whom he worked alongside, left an imprint on all who knew him.
Chris had a passion for music, especially Blues, and attending shows or festivals, and he loved Penn State football. As a nature lover, he lived for bonfires and sunsets, taking road trips and going camping, and even made friends with wild animals like Henry the Turkey. One of his greatest joys was spending time with his children and grandchildren, as well as his dog and beloved companion Forest.
Chris will always be remembered for his courage during difficult times, his willingness to stand up for what he believed in, his positivity and kindness towards everyone, and his love for his family and friends. We find peace knowing he is at rest and one of our guardian angels now.
Chris is survived and missed by his two daughters, Jennifer (Derek) and Heather. He is also survived by three grandchildren Jacob, Caitlyn, and Avyana, his brother Greg (Beth), as well as nephew Scott and niece Carlisle.
Chris was preceded in death by his parents, Lewis & Jean Sanden, and his grandson, Alex.
A Tributes of Life Service and Private interment will be announced at a later time.

Elaine G. Spaulding
BARRE CITY — Elaine Grace Spaulding, 89, a lifelong Barre City resident, passed away on Tuesday, December 30, 2025, at Woodridge Nursing and Rehabilitation Center in Berlin.
Born April 11, 1936, in Barre City, she was the daughter of Frank and Eda (Albinola) Calcagni. Elaine attended elementary school in Barre and graduated from Spaulding High School in 1954.
On June 14, 1958, she married Raymond W. Spaulding at the Hedding United Methodist Church in Barre. All of their married life had been spent in Barre City.
Elaine was a member of the Hedding United Methodist Church of Barre, where she was an active volunteer for many years. Often found in the kitchen, Elaine always looked forward to the Barre Community Christmas dinner, where she worked alongside her family and friends to provide a hot meal and fellowship to those who attended. As consummate volunteers, Raymond and Elaine worked alongside one another throughout the day and would not leave until the last dish had been washed and put away. In addition to her time at Hedding, Elaine was a fixture over the years as both a survivor and volunteer at the Central Vermont Relay for Life. This was a very special cause that she rallied her family around each year, staying up throughout the night, walking laps with her children, grandchildren and friends who could stay awake and match her pace! Always one to put family first, Elaine especially enjoyed the time she spent supporting her grandchildren at the many extracurricular activities they participated in with untold hours spent on fields, in rinks, at pools and in theaters over the years.
Elaine is survived by her children Gary Spaulding (Nancy) of Canterbury, NH; Alison Couture (Richard) and Kevin Spaulding (Sonya) all of Barre, VT; her grandchildren Claire Frances (Jack), Andrew (Samantha), Rachel (Jared), Oliver (Katrina), Parker, Emily Grace, Kyle (Taylor), Molly (Alan) and her great-grandchildren Eden, Camden, Gracen, and Kayden, her brother Robert Calcagni (Deborah) of Florida and her sisters-in-law Sandra Calcagni and Susan Spaulding both of Vermont and her brother-in-law Robert Spaulding also of Vermont as well as six nieces and two nephews.
Elaine was predeceased by her husband, Raymond, her oldest son, Jeffrey, her brother Michael Calcagni, and her brother-in-law, Douglas Spaulding.
A service to honor and celebrate her life will be held on Saturday, February 7, 2026, at 10:30 a.m. at Hooker Whitcomb Funeral Home, 7 Academy Street, Barre. There are no calling hours.
The Spaulding Family would like to thank the caregivers and staff in the Maple Wing at Woodridge Rehabilitation and Nursing who provided a safe and supportive home for Elaine over the last 3 years.
Memorial contributions may be made to Camp Ta-Kum-Ta, PO Box 459, South Hero, VT 05486.
